1.e4 c6 2.Nc3 d5 3.Nf3 Bg4.name: Caro–Kann Defence: Two Knights Attack, Mindeno Variation

1.e4 c6 2.Nc3 d5 3.Nf3 Bg4 4.h3.strategy: Asks the bishop to decide. Black must give up the bishop for the knight and hand White the bishop pair, or retreat and keep the pin, in which case the bishop can be harassed. Either way White gets the choice between quiet and sharp play.

1.e4 c6 2.Nc3 d5 3.Nf3 Bg4 4.h3 Bxf3.strategy: Ends the pin for good by trading the bishop for the knight. Black concedes the bishop pair but keeps a solid pawn structure, so the task is to neutralise the bishops with sound development.
1.e4 c6 2.Nc3 d5 3.Nf3 Bg4 4.h3 Bxf3.name: Caro–Kann Defence: Two Knights Attack, Mindeno Variation, Exchange Line

1.e4 c6 2.Nc3 d5 3.Nf3 Bg4 4.h3 Bh5.strategy: Keeps the bishop and the pin instead of surrendering the bishop pair, but the bishop stands on a square where a pawn push attacks it again and it risks running short of safe squares. Playable, yet Black must be accurate and trading on f3 is simpler.
1.e4 c6 2.Nc3 d5 3.Nf3 Bg4 4.h3 Bh5.name: Caro–Kann Defence: Two Knights Attack, Mindeno Variation, Retreat Line
1.e4 c6 2.Nc3 d5 3.Nf3 Bg4 4.h3 Bh5.background: In Noteboom–Mindeno 1927, Black lost quickly after retreating the bishop to h5.
